medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The University of Oklahoma College of Medicine (OUCOM) is committed to advancing access at all levels. OUCOM recognizes that matriculating talented individuals from widespread backgrounds strongly benefits medical education, patient care, population health, and scientific discovery.

The Office of Access and Community Engagement (ACE) was created to further enhance its commitment to retaining a student body from varied backgrounds. ACE works closely with the University to enhance and preserve access for students and to cultivate meaningful relationships with the surrounding community through outreach initiatives. 

OUCOM directly manages the outreach and retention initiatives for its students by planning, implementing, and evaluating strategies to further a sense of belonging for all students, faculty, and staff.

https://medicine.ouhsc.edu/about/office-of-access-and-community-engagement

Members represent the OU College of Medicine at national, regional, and local conferences, including the Association of American Medical Colleges and the American Medical Association.

medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The University of Oklahoma College of Medicine offers educational tracks in Oklahoma City and Tulsa. 
Unique to the Oklahoma City campus is the opportunity to be a part of a Health Sciences Center, comprised of seven health-related colleges (Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, Pharmacy, Allied Health, Public Health and the Graduate College). Within the campus are multiple centers of excellence and institutes such as the Peggy and Charles Stephenson Cancer Center, the Oklahoma Diabetes Center, the Oklahoma Clinical and Translational Science Institute, the Reynolds Oklahoma Center on Aging, and the Oklahoma Center for Neuroscience.

The OU-TU School of Community Medicine is an integrated track within the OU College of Medicine, which offers all four years on the OU-Tulsa Schusterman Campus. This provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to serve as well-rounded specialty or primary care physicians, while learning a special skill set to improve the health of entire communities.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The newly updated OU College of Medicine curriculum helps students begin mastering the core competencies necessary for medical practice.  Students may select the main Oklahoma City track or the School of Community Medicine track on the Tulsa campus, which includes its own community medicine-focused curriculum.  All students are divided into small-group modules, a unique aspect to our medical school, and engage in learning communities for personal and professional development.  Simulation centers on both campuses provide students with invaluable standardized patient-based learning opportunities throughout the curriculum.

The 18-month preclinical phase begins with Transition to Medical School, providing learning skills and setting the stage for professional success.  The systems-based preclinical curriculum emphasizes integration of basic and clinical science concepts through small- and large-group case-based learning.  Students also have opportunities for clinical and other enrichment experiences in the weeks between their core knowledge-based courses.  This phase ends with Transition to Clerkships to help ensure success in clinical problem-solving, team-based skills, clear communication, quality improvement, and ethical medical practice.

The 12-month clerkship phase offers 7 core clinical clerkships (Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Neurology, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Pediatrics, Psychiatry, and Surgery) plus 3 subspecialty selectives.  In Oklahoma City, there are 4-, 6-, or 8-week block clerkships; in Tulsa, there are year-long longitudinal integrated clerkships (LICs).

The 16-month post-clerkship phase includes a subinternship in each student’s specialty of interest, a plethora of clinical electives, plus a new Transition to Residency course designed to ensure appropriate mastery before entering residency training.  Additionally, preparatory courses for USMLE Step 1 and Step CK are available as electives during the first semester following clerkships
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: On the Tulsa campus, the OU School of Community Medicine provides robust primary care preparation and broad specialty exploration. Students manage a longitudinal patient panel in the Bedlam primary care clinic and may apply to the 3+3 option (accelerated 3 year MD plus residency in Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, or Pediatrics). Graduates enter both primary care and specialties, but the track offers significant opportunities for support in primary care.

Summer research opportunities are also offered through several basic science and clinical departments and the Stephenson Cancer Center. The College of Medicine and the Student Council hold an annual Research Symposium to showcase student research.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The University of Oklahoma College of Medicine offers students a quality education with added advantages. Access to modern patient care facilities and research are provided at a reasonable cost, with a proven record of choice residency placement. Students gain experience in a variety of clinical settings. The college is part of a modern health sciences complex that serves as the state's principal education and research facility for physicians, dentists, nurses, biomedical scientists, pharmacists, public health and allied health professionals. 

OUCOM also includes a School of Community Medicine (SCM) track located in Tulsa, OK. The SCM delivers an LCME-recognized 4-year track (with a 3-year accelerated option) emphasizing community medicine, and supplemental curricular experiences in population health, leadership and advocacy, lifestyle and culinary medicine, and longitudinal care. The SCM  partners with Tulsa hospital systems to prepare students for primary care and specialties.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Our mission is to be the premier institution for advancing medical care, education and research in the state, and to be among the leaders nationally. Our goals are Uncompromising Quality, Exceptional Service, Innovative Education, Advancing Knowledge, and Institutional Strength.

Our Vision: To be a top-tier, research-intensive college of medicine

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
Applicant files may include a maximum of 8 letters of recommendation.

All primary application updates must be submitted via AMCAS by or before October 15 of the current year in order to be considered.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
All letters of recommendation must be received via AMCAS® letter service. 
Three letters of evaluation should be sent from individuals who are familiar with the applicant's recent scientific work, study experience, or professional experience. If a pre-medical committee letter is received, it will count as two of these three letters.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
Applicants are scheduled for a 75-minute virtual interview with members of the OU College of Medicine Admissions Interview Subcommittee. Interview day begins with a required online orientation session followed by preparation logistics of the interview experience. 

Applicants invited to interview are additionally invited to an on-campus, optional group tour, where they will hear details about both OU College of Medicine tracks, which includes the Tulsa campus School of Community Medicine. Applicants will also interact with current medical students, learn about interview day details, and tour the Oklahoma City comprehensive health campus. Tours are also available for the Tulsa campus.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Applicants interview with members of the MD Admissions Interview Subcommittee, a group that includes faculty of the College of Medicine, practicing community physicians, and senior year medical students.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Interviews for the School of Community Medicine track located in Tulsa, OK, are extended by invitation-only.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews are conducted virtually via Zoom.

medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Mission-Aligned Review Process
The College of Medicine utilizes a holistic decision-making process that combines both cognitive and non-cognitive metrics to make admission decisions. 

Screening of Applicants and Granting of Interviews
The College of Medicine Admissions Board has established the following process and criteria that the Office of Admissions follows in the granting of interviews:

The Office of Admissions - Admissions Committee screens all eligible applicants who meet the minimum application requirements. 

The cognitive score shall be a combination of an applicant’s most recent Medical College Admissions Test® (MCAT®) score (no older than two (2) years from the application year) and BCPM grade point average (GPA) as presented on the applicant’s AMCAS® verified application.

If an applicant attends an undergraduate/graduate institution that does not calculate a GPA for all coursework that AMCAS® uses to calculate the BCPM GPA, the applicant’s cognitive score shall be based solely on the MCAT® score.

Non-resident applicants will be granted an interview, inclusive of the above process. In addition, non-resident applicant applications are reviewed for ties to the state of Oklahoma. These ties include, but are not limited to, previous residence in Oklahoma, attendance at an Oklahoma undergraduate college, or family members living in Oklahoma. Oklahoma ties are not required in order to receive an interview.

A sufficient number of interview offers are extended annually between August and January to ensure an adequate class size. The number of interview offers varies by application year.

No applicant is guaranteed an interview.


Interview Process and Scoring
An interview score will be generated by members of the admissions interview subcommittee following completion of the applicant's interview. To be further considered for acceptance, an applicant must obtain a minimum interview score, established annually by the College of Medicine Admissions Board. 

All interviewed applicants will be ranked on a scale using a weighted formula (pre-determined by the Admissions Board) of the combined cognitive and interview scores.

medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
A doctor of medicine degree certifies that a graduate has attained a broad base of knowledge in medicine and the basic skills required for entry into residency training and medical licensure. Faculty deliver a program and curriculum in which students are required to demonstrate competency in the areas of medical knowledge, patient care, communication and interpersonal skills, professionalism, practice-based learning and improvement, and system-based practice.

The purpose of this policy is to set forth the technical standards, which, in conjunction with the published academic standards, are required for admission to, retention and promotion within, and graduation from The University of Oklahoma College of Medicine MD Program.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The MD/PhD program provides training for individuals with strong clinical and basic science interests for research careers in academic medicine. The dual degree program consists of four years of medical school and a minimum of three years of graduate study (which occurs between the preclinical and clinical curricula) including dissertation research in an area of basic biomedical science leading to a PhD degree. 

The work must be conducted under the guidance of a funded clinical and/or basic science investigator who is a member of the Graduate Faculty. The program concludes with clinical clerkships during the final two years of medical school. 

Students will receive academic counseling, career guidance, and participate in special seminars and retreats designed to enhance the educational environment. 

All enrolled MD/PhD students receive a stipend plus full tuition throughout their training.

medSchoolPrograms.cname: Education, Training and Career Enhancement Core - OU Health Stephenson Cancer Center

medSchoolPrograms.info:
To provide additional opportunities for students to round out their education and pursue areas of interest, OU College of Medicine offers these special programs:

International Studies in Medicine
Current fourth-year College of Medicine students in good academic standing are eligible to apply for an opportunity to participate in an international rotation at an affiliated program. Support funding for the international rotation may be available, but not all students who apply to the international program may receive the funding.

A fourth-year student may only participate in an international rotation during September or February of the fourth-year. A rotation at an international affiliated program is considered on-campus.  

https://medicine.ouhsc.edu/prospective-students/special-programs

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: The OU School of Community Medicine track in Tulsa offers a three-year MD pathway for students committed to primary care and community‑focused specialties. Students may express interest during the admissions process, but selection into the pathway occurs during the first year of medical school based on academic readiness, professionalism, and specialty alignment. The accelerated curriculum includes year‑round coursework, early clinical immersion, and competency‑based progression.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
By Oklahoma State Regents for Higher Education Policy, all applicants must have a minimum total GPA of 3.0 and a minimum total MCAT score of 492 to be eligible applicants. Prerequisite courses must have a letter grade of "C" or better.  

Pass/Fail grading, advanced placement, and CLEP courses are accepted if a subsequent higher course is taken for a grade. 

Please note that the above are minimums and considered non-competitive.

medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
Decisions are based on an applicant's indications and probabilities of successfully completing medical school, relevant intellectual competencies, academic achievement, character, motivation, and maturity. The assessment utilizes college grades, MCAT scores, letters of recommendation, personal statements, and results of the required interview. 

Intellectual competency and academic achievement alone are not sufficient to assure the professional development and commitment required of medical school or a physician. Traits of personality, maturity,  varied backgrounds, and character are necessary to communicate warmth, compassion, and to work effectively in a profession dependent upon interpersonal relationships, cross cultural appreciation, and high ethical behavior.  

The University of Oklahoma College of Medicine does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, creed, national origin, age, or handicap.
